IRT checks for the item-revision loop

Source: R/loop-steps.R
loop_irt.Rd

loop_irt() makes the evaluator step of revision_loop(). For every scale, it fits a unidimensional IRT model with mirt to the keyed answers of the round. By default this is the partial credit model (Masters, 1982), a Rasch model for ordered categories with every slope fixed at 1; model = "gpcm" (generalized partial credit) and model = "graded" (graded response) estimate a slope per item instead. It flags

Usage

loop_irt(
  model = c("pcm", "gpcm", "graded"),
  thresholds = list(),
  itemfit = TRUE,
  q3 = TRUE,
  overfit = c("fail", "warn")
)

Arguments

model

the IRT model: "pcm" (partial credit, the default), "gpcm" (generalized partial credit) or "graded" (graded response).

thresholds

a named list that changes any of the defaults list(msq = c(0.6, 1.4), misfit_p = 0.01, slope = 0.65, steep = 4, q3 = 0.2, info = NULL).

itemfit, q3

compute the item fit statistics and the Q3 residuals? They are the slowest parts.

overfit

severity of a mean square below the range (answers more predictable than the model expects): "fail" or "warn". Language models often answer almost deterministically for a given persona, which rewording cannot change, so "warn" lets the stopping rule rest on the other checks.

Value

A function for the evaluator argument of revision_loop().

Details

  • msq_misfit (fail, partial credit model): Infit or outfit mean square outside thresholds$msq (0.6 to 1.4 by default, the range Wright and Linacre (1994) give for rating scales). Below the range, answers are more predictable than the model expects (often a sign of redundant items or tidy synthetic respondents); above it, they are noisy. With overfit = "warn", an item that is only too predictable is a warning, and only noisy items fail.

  • misfit (fail): The S-X2 item fit test (Orlando & Thissen, 2000) has a p value below thresholds$misfit_p.

  • disordered (warn): The item's thresholds (the points where one category becomes more likely than the one below) are not in increasing order, so some categories are never the most likely answer.

  • low_slope (fail, "gpcm" and "graded" only): A discrimination below thresholds$slope; a negative slope means the item runs against its scale.

  • steep_slope (warn, "gpcm" and "graded" only): A discrimination above thresholds$steep, which synthetic respondents that answer almost deterministically produce.

  • local_dependence (warn): The item's largest Q3 residual correlation (Yen, 1984) exceeds the mean Q3 of its scale by more than thresholds$q3, a sign that two items share more than the trait.

  • no_variance (fail): Every respondent gives the same answer, so the item cannot be fitted.

  • low_info (fail, only with thresholds$info): The mean test information of the scale between theta -2 and 2 is below the target.

  • irt_failed (fail): The model could not be fitted for the scale.

Stats: Per item location (the mean of its thresholds), infit and outfit (partial credit model), slope ("gpcm" and "graded") and sx2_p, and per scale info_mean and marginal_rxx (marginal reliability), which loop_criterion() can use as targets, for example min = list(marginal_rxx = 0.8). Both are taken over the estimated latent distribution, with the trait standardized: info_mean is the mean information between 2 SD below and 2 SD above the latent mean, and marginal_rxx is the mean of \(\sigma^2 I / (\sigma^2 I + 1)\). With a latent variance of 1 these equal the usual values.

References

Masters, G. N. (1982). A Rasch model for partial credit scoring. Psychometrika, 47(2), 149-174.

Orlando, M., & Thissen, D. (2000). Likelihood-based item-fit indices for dichotomous item response theory models. Applied Psychological Measurement, 24(1), 50-64.

Wright, B. D., & Linacre, J. M. (1994). Reasonable mean-square fit values. Rasch Measurement Transactions, 8(3), 370.

Yen, W. M. (1984). Effects of local item dependence on the fit and equating performance of the three-parameter logistic model. Applied Psychological Measurement, 8(2), 125-145.

See also

revision_loop(), loop_checker()

Examples

# \donttest{
h <- hexaco_items[hexaco_items$facet %in% c("HSinc", "HFair"), ]
ca <- hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ]
irt <- loop_irt()
out <- irt(ca[1:400, ], h, list(construct = loop_construct("H", scale = c(1, 7))))
out$flags
